newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK JUNE EXPORTS UP 23 PCT TO $2.1 BLN-EXPORTERS.
newsitem.headline: TURK JUNE EXPORTS UP 23 PCT TO $2.1 BLN-EXPORTERS.

text.p: Turkey's exports jumped by 23 percent to $2.11 billion in June from $1.72 billion a year earlier, despite political turmoil, the Turkish Exporters' Assembly (TIM) said on Friday.
Exports for the first six months of this year rose 15 percent to $12.61 billion from $10.92 billion in the same period of 1996.
Conservative politician Mesut Yilmaz was appointed prime minister at the end of June after the resignation of Islamist leader Necmettin Erbakan, ending weeks of speculation and uncertainty.

Exports by Turkey's leading clothing sector increased by 27 percent last month from June 1996 to $555 million, followed by iron and steel exports which gained 29 percent to $282.8 million and textile and related raw materials which were up 34 percent to $237.5 million.
The largest jump in June exports was recorded by tobacco, which soared 122 percent from a year ago to $45.7 million.

Compared to June 1996, electrical and electronic exports were up 26 percent to $196.3 million, grain, pulse and oilseed exports up 51 percent to $144.5 million and automotive exports edged up two percent to $122.6 million, TIM said.

In the first six months of 1997, clothing exports rose 20 percent to $3.4 billion, iron and steel exports stood at $1.6 billion and textile and related raw material products at $1.3 billion, both up 14 percent from the same period in 1996.
